payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image, with its front panels meeting or overlapping throughout the full intended closure?
node.criteria: Identify the intended front closure and inspect its upper, middle, and lower portions wherever visible. Pass only if visible evidence establishes continuous meeting or overlap of the front panels throughout the full intended closure, with no unclosed segment. Fail if any clearly visible segment of that closure remains open, even if other segments are obscured or closed. Unknown if no open segment is established but pose, drape, occlusion, or insufficient detail prevents establishing full closure. Outward-hanging fabric, folds, a loose hem, changed silhouette, or absence of a clearly visible gap alone establishes neither full closure nor an open segment.
node.binding: Use the woman's jacket in the SOURCE image as the garment reference and assess that same jacket in the EDITED image against the requested fully closed state. Locate the source jacket's front-panel edges and intended closure extent, then compare corresponding garment features and inspect any visible portions of the front-panel meeting line in the edited image, accounting for the changed pose. Do not substitute the outer silhouette for closure evidence. Unrelated changes do not satisfy this condition.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the jacket’s front panels separated, with a clearly visible open gap down the front; they do not meet or overlap throughout the closure.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding and criterion already target the correct garment and require visible evidence of full closure; the trace reports a clear open gap, which is negative visual evidence, not a transport or dependency failure. However, the rubric distinguishes partial progress from no progress, while this single binary check only tests complete closure. It cannot tell whether the jacket was partly closed, so its “no” may incorrectly drive the aggregate despite the reference label. Preserve the full-closure check, but make the decision output or downstream evaluation separately capture observable partial progress (for example, whether any portion of the intended closure has moved toward meeting), and reserve “no progress” for evidence that no requested change occurred. Do not infer progress from pose or silhouette alone; compare corresponding closure features in source and edited images, and use unresolved when visibility prevents that comparison. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this jacket is fully closed."}
